entities.name: PMID:25442036
observations: Shaitelman et al. reported clinical outcomes from the multicenter Contura multilumen balloon breast brachytherapy Phase IV registry trial.
The cohort included 342 evaluable patients from 23 institutions, enrolled January 2008 to February 2011, treated with 34 Gy in 10 twice-daily fractions.
Median follow-up was 36 months (range 1–54 months); 3-year local recurrence-free survival was 97.8%.
The report included 10 ipsilateral breast tumor recurrences, 88% good-to-excellent cosmesis, 8.5% infection, 4.4% symptomatic seroma, uncommon grade 3 toxicity, and no grade 4 toxicity.
No mature 5-year-or-longer clinical outcomes were identified for this registry cohort in the searched evidence.

entities.name: PMID:21925955
observations: A separate 46-patient single-institution Contura series reported median 36-month follow-up, one local recurrence, 4.3% persistent seroma, 2.2% telangiectasia, no grade III toxicity, and 97% good/excellent cosmesis at 36 months.
This study is not the multicenter Phase IV registry cohort.

entities.name: Contura follow-up maturity
observations: The Contura Phase IV registry has published intermediate-term clinical outcomes, but the located evidence does not establish mature long-term follow-up at 5 years or more.

entities.name: Major depressive disorder
observations: Current depressive episode is suggested by depressed mood, low motivation, impaired concentration, hypersomnia, increased appetite, leaden limb sensation, and functional impairment lasting about one month.
Atypical depressive features include hypersomnia, increased appetite or weight gain, leaden paralysis, and mood reactivity; seasonal recurrence is a related specifier rather than required here.

entities.name: Seasonal pattern
observations: Increased frequency of depressive symptoms during winter is characteristic of a seasonal pattern and is the best listed feature compatible with this presentation.
